Field notes

What a small bakery taught us about queues

Three months behind the counter, and one spreadsheet.

Most mornings the line formed before the doors opened. People waited longer on Saturdays, but they complained more on Tuesdays, when the wait was shorter and nobody expected it.

We started writing down every order with a timestamp. By the end of the first month the pattern was obvious: the bottleneck was never the oven.

The bottleneck was the till

Card payments took twice as long as cash, mostly because of the receipt printer.

We moved the printer and the line shrank by a third.

  • Move the printer next to the till
  • Pre-pack the three most common orders
    • Croissant and coffee
    • Two baguettes
  • Open the second till at 8:00

None of these cost money. All of them came from writing things down.
